newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Oct 18.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Oct 18.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

As the Federal Government continued to come under fire from compromises in Ministerial standards yesterday, Industry Minister John Moore dumped his 42,400 remaining shares in Bligh Ventures and Finance Minister John Fahey resigned his undeclared interests as director and shareholder of Tunboa Pty Ltd, a small private firm. Page 1.

In the lead-up to the Lindsay by-election, Prime Minister John Howard yesterday accused Opposition Leader Kim Beazley of hypocrisy over the issue of racism. Howard claimed Labor was involved in a "sleazy" preferences deal with controversial Lindsay candidates from the Australians Against Further Immigration party. Page 2.

The New South Wales Anti-Discrimination Board's annual report has shown there has been a 51 per cent increase in racial discrimination complaints and a 25 per cent increase in complaints from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders during the past year. Page 4.

The Australian Industrial Relations Commission has paved the way for the Community and Public Sector Union to seek Federal award rates for tens of thousands of State public sector workers in all States. The CPSU moved immediately to apply to the IRC for a number of benefits the Victorian Government abolished in late 1992. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard has apologised to the Australian public for the breaches in Ministerial standards that have plagued his front bench over the past week. Howard said he was sorry that a number of people had been careless and had embarrassed his Government by failing to divest shareholdings. The latest to succumb to pressure over the share revelations, Industry Minister John Moore, yesterday sold shares worth over A$80,000. Page 1.

Up to 110,000 State public servants can now apply for Federal awards. The Industrial Relations Commission yesterday made the decision which allows unions to purse Federal award rates, which in general have better pay and conditions. Page 1.

Under a radical health shake-up, Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett will close 10 Melbourne hospitals and five more will be shifted or downgraded. Kennett claimed his was the only Government that had the courage to attempt the reforms while the Opposition deounced the move as being "a black day for Victoria". Page 1.

Federal Parliament was yesterday told a male staff member of controversial Independent MP Pauline Hanson had threatened and sexually harassed a female Liberal MP staffer. However, the allegations, made by Gary Hardgrave MP, were challenged by Hanson's only staff member, John Pasquarelli, who demanded Hardgrave make the claims outside Parliament House. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Prime Minister John Howard has apologised to Australians for the "careless" behaviour of some of his Ministers and their breaches of the code of conduct. Meanwhile, Finance Minister John Fahey yesterday admitted to being negligent in maintaining his New South Wales pecuniary interest register. Page 1.

It has been revealed Employment Minister Amanda Vanstone ignored her department's advice to publicly correct claims that a millionaire family had rorted welfare benefits. The Department of Employment Education and Youth Affairs wrote to Vanstone a day aftr the "Wright" story appeared in the media, advising her to retract the claims made in the press. Page 2.

An 82-year-old woman suffered a broken nose, fractured cheekbone and blackened eyes when she was repeatedly punched by a youth outside her home. The offender stole the woman's bag, which contained a purse holding only $6. Page 3.

After two years, New South Wales' water restrictions were lifted yesterday, once again allowing Sydney-siders to do what they please with water. The restrictions started after the State's worst drought, when water supplies fell to a record low of 55.6 percent in 1994. Page 3.
THE AGE

In unprecedented reforms to the Victorian Health System, six hospitals will close and three will be built in growth areas. Although A$900 million will be spent on new health facilities over the next decade, up to 400 hospital beds will disappear and Melbourne's Alfred, St Vincent's and Royal Melbourne Hospitals are ear-marked to be scaled down. Page A1

The Federal Government's share woes shifted to Victoria yesterday when the State's Attorney-General, Jan Wade, was under pressure to resign after it was revealed she ruled out a contempt of court action mounted against BHP earlier this year while holding more than A$12,000 worth of shares in the company. Page A1.

Melbourne's secondary airport, Essendon, is likely to be closed before the sale of Tullamarine Airport. The Federal Government decision follows Essendon's increasing losses, declining air traffic and major safety concerns. Page A3.

The Victorian Government's industrial relations system was in turmoil last night with a landmark Industrial Relations Commission ruling paving the way for all Australian public sector members to work under the Federal award structure. The IRC decision allows over 100,000 in Victoria, South Australia, Western Australia and Queensland to apply for interim Federal awards. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
